value.rationale: Kemeny constants are meaningful network navigation/performance summaries. Identical stationary state frequencies, full per-state sojourn laws and fresh-entrance mean hitting times would normally be considered sufficient reduced network statistics. The matched pair proves this information cannot determine the average random-target time from a random physical-time observation, and detects a sign reversal that unmarked variability (each CV squared equals one) entirely misses. Three states are minimal for a pure destination-marking effect without self-jumps, making a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary isolated number. The exact general formula identifies the missing first marked moments.
